title: Review of pcell-multilevel (S,I,D,H): selection on yield by intrinsic deaths replicates on fresh seeds 5 and 6, and low yield precedes death by 5000-10000 t; no population-mean response (Supported, with that limit)
summary: Looked at sel_vs_marker.png and the pack sheets, then ran the claimed world.py on fresh seeds 5 and 6 with the author's genealogy.py (T=100000) and a labkit run on seed 5 (rerun/seed5: 20 persistent splits, generation 3, 1 merge). Dying mature cells sit at the 2.6th and 4.4th yield percentile of the living cells (39/39 and 23/24 below the median) while the inert marker carried by the same particles sits at 0.69 and 0.42; splitting cells are above the median in yield (0.63, 0.77; marker 0.44, 0.55); daughters keep the parent's yield (r = 0.84, 0.88; mean |change| 0.022-0.025 vs between-cell SD 0.10-0.13). To test whether low yield causes death or only appears while a cell dies, lagsel.py reads each dying cell's yield percentile some time before its death: 5000 t before, doomed cells were already at 0.14-0.22 on all five seeds (author's 0-2 and my 5-6; 20-28 of 22-29 below the median), 10000 t before at 0.20-0.31, and only at 20000 t before do they approach 0.35-0.44; the marker stays at 0.40-0.69 throughout (except the author's seed 2, 0.25-0.47). So low-yield cells are marked for death well in advance, which supports cell-level selection rather than a collapse artefact.

observations.S: rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=0: uniform particle soup and noisy phi, no planted cells; ~25 cells by t=4000
observations.I: rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=4000-100000: discrete bounded walled cells
observations.D: rerun/seed5/FACTS.md: 20 persistent splits, max generation 3, 1 merge; data/gen_s5.log and gen_s6.log: 28 and 27 particle-genealogy splits, generation 5 and 6
observations.H: data/selection_review.txt: death yield percentile 0.026 and 0.044 (marker 0.69, 0.42), split percentile 0.63 and 0.77, parent-daughter r 0.84 and 0.88 on fresh seeds 5 and 6; lag 5000: 0.15 and 0.14

controls_run.H: inert marker zm of the same particles in the same runs (data/selection_review.txt), and the lagged readout lagsel.py on the author's seeds 0-2 and my seeds 5-6

verdicts.limitation: The trait is continuous and the 'kinds' are yield ranks; the population-mean yield does not clearly rise (the author reports +0.07 to +0.16 within the marker's drift), consistent with within-cell cheater evolution balancing between-cell selection, so this is a selection differential with heredity, not a demonstrated response. The marker is not an independent identical-event twin run and can hitchhike (author's seed 2). One cost value.
